newsitem.title: POLAND: LESS THAN HALF OF POLES HAVE ANY SAVINGS - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: LESS THAN HALF OF POLES HAVE ANY SAVINGS - SURVEY.

text.p: Only about 45 percent of Polish urban households have any savings and only about 35 percent use banking credit, a survey published on Wednesday showed.

The poll of 1,279 households was commissioned by state-owned Bank PKO BP and Bank Zachodni SA banks and Polcard payment card distributor and carried out by a research institution affiliated with the Polish Banking Association.
Bogumila Swat of Zachodni's research department, told a news conference the survey, conducted in October, allowed banks to better define market needs and areas which should be developed.
The survey showed most polled households had little knowledge of banking products, investment opportunities and most were reluctant to borrow from banks.
"15,8 percent of those surveyed declared they would invest in bonds and stocks if they had more money but most savings are used for consumption," said Andrzej Ochocki, the survey's co-author.
Only seven percent of those surveyed declared they could live on their savings for more than a year and about 20 percent said their spare money would suffice for more than a month.
Out of those who said they were not using banking credit 29.6 percent said one should avoid borrowing at all, 21.3 percent saw no such need and 26.2 percent said interest rates were too high.
The poll also showed that despite consumer credit boom, which saw it doubling last year, longer term credits were still scarce because of high interest rates and relatively low incomes.
